title: Tiered optimizer operational runbook: automated batching & cache recommendations with safe apply/rollback
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem statement: We need an operationally safe system that generates per-customer and per-route batching/caching recommendations, can autonomously apply them where allowed, and automatically rollback when customer-facing quality or reliability regressions are detected. The system must support tier-based controls (free/standard/premium), allowlists/denylists for special customers/routes, and provide explainable recommendations plus a simulation/dry-run path before any live change.

Why now: token costs and latency variability continue to be a top customer complaint and expense vector. Several large customers have bespoke needs (low-latency vs. low-cost) that require deterministic per-tenant controls. Automation will reduce manual ops load and surface cost-saving opportunities consistently across routes.

Scope: build the core recommendation engine, simulation harness, safe-apply pipeline (dry-run -> canary -> ramp -> monitor), automatic rollback triggers, per-tenant allow/deny rule layer, and operational docs/runbook for SE/Support to interpret events and intervene. This ticket covers engineering design, implementation plan, instrumentation, and an initial rollout for beta customers (tenants in the Early Adopters tier).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Recommendation engine produces deterministic batching and cache TTL suggestions per (customer, route) and exposes confidence scores and rationale strings
A2: Simulation mode can run recommendations on 30 days of historical traces and produce an estimated cost delta and latency impact report
A3: Safe-apply pipeline implements four-stage rollout (dry-run, 1% canary tenants, 25% ramp, full) with abort and automatic rollback hooks
A4: Rollback triggers defined and implemented: p95 latency increase > 15% above baseline OR error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR quality regression metric (prompt-level eval) degrades by > 3 points
A5: Admin UI and CLI show per-tenant applied profile, allowlist/denylist membership, recent rollouts, and last rollback reason
A6: Audit logs are emitted for every policy change with actor, rationale link, affected tenants/routes, and config diff
A7: Unit + e2e tests cover recommendation scoring, dry-run simulator, apply/rollback orchestration, and safety gate conditions
implementation_steps: Step 1: Design recommendation schema: rules for batching window, max batch size, KV cache TTL, prefix cache window, and model-variant preference. Include fields for confidence, provenance, and simulated impact estimates.

Step 2: Build offline simulator that replays historical request traces, applies candidate configs, and measures delta on tokens, p95 latency, cache hit rate, and downstream evals. Store results as a report artifact.
Step 3: Implement allowlist/denylist service layer: tenant-level and route-level entries with precedence rules, timeboxed entries, and owner metadata.
Step 4: Create safe-apply orchestration: dry-run (no-op with logs), canary selector (deterministic hashing), ramp scheduler, circuit-breaker for rollbacks, and reconciliation loop.
Step 5: Integrate with rollout & config service: atomic config commits, feature-flag gating for auto-apply, and rollback API endpoints.
Step 6: Instrument telemetry: per-tenant token usage, per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit rates, batch sizes, per-request model variant, and quality eval hooks for sampled prompts.
Step 7: Create incident/resolution playbook: on rollback, capture snapshot of request traces, compare simulator vs. live delta, notify SE/CS, and open follow-up action item.
Step 8: Build admin console views and CLI commands for: preview recommendations, schedule rollout, force rollback, edit allowlist/denylist, and export runbook reports.
Step 9: Run pilot with 5 early-adopter tenants, collect telemetry for 7 days, refine thresholds and confidence heuristics, then expand tiered rollout rules for Standard customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positive recommendations could increase latency or reduce perceived quality. Mitigation: require simulation pass and human approval for high-confidence changes on high-impact tenants; enforce canary and slow ramp schedules.
Risk: Noisy telemetry leads to spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: use aggregated windows (5m & 1h) and require sustained breach across both windows before rollback; add anomaly-suppression smoothing.

Risk: Multi-tenant fairness/regulatory concerns when optimizing for cost. Mitigation: expose per-tenant opt-out, require legal review for tenant-level weight shifting, and log all policy decisions for audits.
Risk: Race conditions during concurrent rollouts. Mitigation: serializable config commits with per-tenant locks and optimistic concurrency checks; reconcile loop fixes drift.
Risk: Secret/key leaks in audit artifacts. Mitigation: redact PII/keys in reports and enforce access controls on runbook artifacts.
outage_and_rollback_playbook: If rollback trigger fires during canary or ramp: immediately mark the rollout as aborted, initiate automatic rollback to last known good config, notify on-call, and create incident ticket with simulator vs live comparison.
If rollback occurs after full rollout: pause auto-apply globally, notify PM/SE for impacted tenants, and schedule emergency hotfix window to iterate on recommendation heuristics.
Manual rollback steps: CLI `ri rollout rollback --id <rollout-id>` -> wait for config reconciliation -> run diagnostic script to collect traces and evaluation samples -> assign owner for follow-up.
Post-rollback review: within 48 hours produce a remediation doc with root cause, simulator discrepancy, and updated guardrails.
metrics_to_track: Per-route p95 latency and p99 latency
Average and median batch size achieved
notification_and_alerting: Create an Alert: cost-automation.rollback-trigger fired -> PagerDuty to inference-oncall
Create a Ticket: any automatic rollback generates a templated issue in Linear assigned to the rollout owner
Slack digest: daily summary of recommendations applied, cost delta estimates, and outstanding approvals
Email to SE/CS: weekly report for tenants in Early Adopter cohort
notes: This runbook intentionally separates the recommendation generation from the apply path. Short term we will keep auto-apply disabled for Premium and some regulated customers; long term we may enable opt-in auto-apply for Standard tier after 30d of stable metrics. The simulation harness should be made reusable for other optimization features (model-variant recommendations, quantization profiles).
